notes:
Batch-repair read pipeline fix: the read window now scales with batch size, expired rows tell the truth, and large batches split into bounded requests.

Why: on 2026-10-17 a production batch repair created from the deep audit (14 pages) stuck permanently at the "read site state" step. Diagnosis, all read-only from production: each target page becomes one preparation row whose window was a fixed 5-minute TTL; the outbound runner claims one preparation per ~22-second poll and each page read takes 25-120 seconds, so six items was marginal and fifteen items was mathematically impossible to finish in one window. Rows that expired while still queued were never marked in any way (25 dead rows had accumulated), and the review UI displayed every queued row as "waiting for executor" regardless of expiry, so work that had already expired looked like it was still in flight. One Bridge read additionally hung for 5m22s and was SIGTERMed by systemd, wasting a whole window.

What changes, three connected fixes in one release. (1) The preparation window scales with batch size: max(5 minutes, items x 90 seconds), capped at 30 minutes; the stored result validity now follows the batch window (min of the row window and the runner-declared expiry) instead of a fixed 5-minute constant, because otherwise the pages read first expire before the batch finishes and a large batch can never become fully usable for candidate generation. (2) Honest display: preparation views now carry a server-derived displayStatus (usable / waiting / expired / needs_reread, with expiry checked before in-flight) and the review workspace shows a progress counter ("snapshot progress: X/N usable") plus per-item "expired, re-read required" for dead rows, instead of the previous permanent "waiting for executor". (3) Automatic splitting: the from-findings endpoint now splits a batch of more than 10 pages into multiple requests of 10 pages each - 10 pages is 11 items, about a 16.5-minute window, the balance point between read cadence, snapshot freshness and hang tolerance. Splitting does not change authorization semantics: each request still requires its own approval and confirmation, and the rollup panel now shows per-batch links instead of silently navigating into the first batch. The request-level page cap rises from 16 to 50 (five requests).

Database: no migrations. The schema stays at 052 as applied by v0.2.29; an upgrade from v0.2.29 does not need the worker/dispatcher stop that a migration-bearing upgrade requires.

Rollback target: v0.2.29 application images only. Nothing persisted changes shape - the window is computed per batch at prepare time and displayStatus is derived at read time and never stored - so a rollback needs no data action. Preparation rows created by the new code may carry longer expiries; the previous code reads them correctly (it only compares them to the current time).

Bootstrap: unchanged from v0.2.29.

Validation before tagging, on a clean worktree of commit a87992c (subsequent commits add only evidence files and this manifest): pnpm install --frozen-lockfile; pnpm --filter api test 2122 passed / 189 skipped / 0 failed (the four newly skipped are the PostgreSQL-gated suites the disposable verifier runs for real); pnpm typecheck zero errors; pnpm build; the BFF routing verification 124/124 across the ip, domain and tunnel Caddy templates (real Caddy v2.10.2 -> built Next BFF -> synthetic API); the full CI bootstrap-contract block including the 23 Python retention cases; git diff --check clean. Batch-specific: the disposable PostgreSQL 16 verifier ran migrations twice and the 6 default suites 132/132 in both the main tree and the clean worktree; before the fixes the same suites ran red at 4 failed / 128 passed with the new tests failing for exactly the intended reasons (fixed 300000 vs expected 990000, missing displayStatus, no split fields). The entry-UI browser drill against the real components passed 46/46 with no browser errors and no external requests, including the new split-branch checks. The main working tree additionally runs 48 tests from another session's uncommitted WordPress files (2170 passed / 189 skipped there), which this release does not contain.

Not asserted here: a production end-to-end batch read. The real acceptance is the user retrying the read on the production batch request; the fixes are covered end-to-end by the disposable-PostgreSQL suites (route split with independent audit rows, TTL 990s for an 11-item batch, result validity equal to the row window, the displayStatus state machine) and by the browser drill against the real entry components.
